about.title: Westmorland Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Westmorland is small enough that a loss is felt on nearly every block. With a population of about 2,267, word travels quickly when a family loses a parent, a child or a spouse, and the grief spreads well past one household. Public records for 2024 list two injury collisions and no traffic deaths within the city, yet a wrongful death claim rarely turns on a single year's totals. Fatal crashes on Route 85 or along W Main Street, a fall at a worksite in the surrounding fields, a medical mistake at a clinic across Imperial County, a defective product in the home — any of these can give rise to a civil claim when someone else's negligence caused the death. California limits who may bring that claim, sets a two-year deadline that shrinks sharply when a public agency is involved, and allows recovery for funeral costs, lost financial support and the loss of companionship and guidance. LawProactive simply connects Westmorland families with an independent attorney who handles these cases, at no cost and without pressure.

whyChoose.title: Why Westmorland Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California gives a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain dependents and heirs eligible in other situations. The attorney you're matched with can sort out where your family stands.

items.title: The two-year clock is watched
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window narrows considerably when a city, county or state agency is involved. Early contact keeps those deadlines from slipping by while you grieve.

items.title: Every loss is accounted for
items.desc: Recoverable losses reach beyond funeral and burial costs to include the financial support the person would have provided and the love, companionship and guidance your family has lost. Network attorneys handle these cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Westmorland recorded zero traffic deaths in 2024. Does that mean wrongful death cases don't happen here?
items.answer: Not at all. A single year's count within city limits doesn't capture deaths on the county roads and highways just outside town, nor does it include workplace incidents, medical errors, or product failures. Families here have the same rights under California law as anyone else in Imperial County, regardless of how quiet a given year looks on paper.

items.question: The person responsible is facing criminal charges. Do we still need a civil case?
items.answer: Yes, they are separate matters. A criminal case is brought by the state to punish wrongdoing, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the family to recover its losses. One can move forward regardless of how the other turns out, and the outcome of the criminal case does not decide the civil claim.

items.question: Our loved one died in a crash involving a county vehicle. Is the timeline different?
items.answer: It usually is. When a government entity may be responsible, California requires a formal claim to be presented much sooner than the general two-year deadline, and missing that step can end the case before it begins. An attorney can identify every party involved and make sure the shorter notice requirements are met.
